tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description:
Get the top-ranked prediction market traders (grades S, A, B only). Sorted by composite score descending. Supports cursor pagination and optional filters.

Args:
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20): Max results per page
  - cursor (string, optional): Pagination cursor from previous response
  - category (string, optional): Filter by category slug
  - strategy (string, optional): Current styles: two_sided, category_focused, high_activity, diversified, mixed, unclassified. Historical filters remain accepted: accumulator, algo_trader, arbitrageur, directional, event_driven, market_maker, momentum, scalper, speculator, swing_trader

Returns: Ranked list of traders with grade, score, P&L, volume, win rate, and strategy.

tools.name: get_trader
tools.description:
Look up a prediction market trader by wallet address or username. Returns grade (S through F), P&L breakdown, win rate, and volume.

Optional expand fields for heavier data:
- strategy: Trading strategy classification
- categories: Per-category performance breakdown
- quant_metrics: curated advanced metrics (copy_score and smart_score 0-100, sharpe_30d, sharpe_7d, profit_factor, edge_consistency, sharpe_percentile, pf_percentile, consistency_percentile); emitted only for a computed row strictly under six hours old, otherwise omitted; each present value is a number or null
- trust: Per-field provenance (source, freshness, reconciliation, completeness) for grade, P&L, and stats

A wallet address with no trader yet returns sync_status "unknown" (not an error). A username or trader id that matches no trader is a not_found error.

Args:
  - address (string, required): Ethereum wallet address (0x...) or trader username
  - expand (string[], optional): Heavy fields to include: "strategy", "categories", "quant_metrics", "trust"
  - max_age_s (integer, optional, 0 or more): Freshness ceiling in seconds. The call answers only when data_quality.status is fresh and data_quality.as_of is no older than this; otherwise it fails with reason freshness_ceiling_unsatisfied (HTTP 409). Nothing is refreshed to meet it

Returns: Trader profile with grade, P&L, stats, and optional expanded fields. The trader carries data_quality: status, as_of (the oldest clock the body rests on) and field_groups. fresh means tracked and clocked, not current: compare as_of with your own tolerance. unknown means this read cannot date that group, never that it is recent.

address.description: Ethereum wallet address (0x...) or trader username

max_age_s.description: Freshness ceiling in seconds: answer only when data_quality.status is fresh and data_quality.as_of is no older than this, otherwise fail with freshness_ceiling_unsatisfied

tools.name: batch_get_traders
tools.description:
Read-only batch lookup for 1-25 trader wallet addresses or known usernames. Results preserve request order and duplicate inputs return duplicate rows. Uses the same V1 batch item quota as POST /api/v1/traders/batch.

Args:
  - traders (string[], required): Wallet addresses or known usernames
  - expand (string[], optional): Heavy fields to include for every trader: "strategy", "categories", "quant_metrics", "trust" (per-item quant_metrics is omitted unless its computed row is strictly under six hours old; trust is per-field provenance for grade, P&L, and stats)

Returns: Ordered batch trader results with per-item success or error details. Each successful item's trader carries data_quality: status, as_of and field_groups; fresh means tracked and clocked, not current, and unknown means undatable, never recent.

tools.name: get_large_trades
tools.description:
Get recent large trades from graded prediction market traders. Each trade includes a 0-1 review score, persisted suspicion facts, trader grade, and market context. Cursor-paginated, newest first.

Args:
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20): Max results per page
  - cursor (string, optional): Pagination cursor from previous response
  - min_size (number, default 5000): Minimum trade size in USD
  - category (string, optional): Filter by market category (case-insensitive)
  - min_grade (string, optional): Minimum trader grade (S, A, B, C, D, F)
  - suspicious_only (boolean, optional): Keep only persisted suspicion_score >= 60; false preserves the current result set
  - min_market_volume_share (number, 0-1, optional): Keep only trades whose market_volume_share is known and at least this; a fraction, so 0.01 is one percent of the market's traded volume
  - sort (string, optional): "recent" (default, newest first) or "market_volume_share" (biggest share of its market first, over the last 30 days, or from the from bound on the history tools; a cursor is bound to the order it was minted in)
  - since (string, optional): wt_ id of a trade a previous call returned; answers only the trades recorded after it, in commit order, so a trade recorded late still arrives. Poll with the first trade of the last answer that had trades and deduplicate on id; recent order only

Returns: List of large trades with trader info, market context, size, side, price, current review_score (signal_score is its deprecated twin, same value) and trader grade, point-in-time recorded_review_score (recorded_signal_score is its deprecated twin; null before 2026-08-03) and trader grade_at_trade with grade_at_trade_status (unknown before 2026-09-19), optional suspicion_score, and optional suspicion_track. A null suspicion track means the persisted legacy row has no track label. The page carries data_quality beside data: status, as_of (the oldest clock the page rests on) and field_groups. fresh means tracked and clocked, not current: compare as_of with your own tolerance. unknown means this read cannot date that group, never that it is recent.

suspicious_only.description: Keep only rows with persisted suspicion_score >= 60

min_market_volume_share.description: Keep only trades whose market_volume_share is known and at least this. A fraction, not a percent: 0.01 is one percent of the market's traded volume. A trade whose share is unavailable is never returned by a non-zero value

sort.description: Order of the page. recent is newest first. market_volume_share ranks by each trade's share of its market's traded volume, biggest first, a trade whose share is unavailable last, over the last 30 days. A cursor is bound to the order it was minted in

since.description: wt_ id of a trade a previous call returned: answer only the trades recorded after it, in commit order, so a trade recorded late still arrives and none is skipped. Poll with the first trade of the last answer that had trades and deduplicate on id. Recent order only

tools.name: get_edge_hunter
tools.description: Read the Max-only Edge Hunter API at https://0xinsider.com/sports/edge. Pro receives 403 forbidden with reason max_plan_required. One view selector offers board (default), full signals and cohort observations. All views accept kind sports|esports (omission covers both), sports, leagues, market_types, condition_ids, event_slugs, series_slugs and legacy category. Array selections accept 1..100 supplied values before deduplication, including comma-separated values inside a value; repeat REST query keys or supply MCP arrays. Lists match OR; axes match AND. Canonical sports and machine league identities normalize case-insensitively; market types and event/series slugs are exact case-sensitive provider strings. category=NFL selects the Football bucket; leagues=[nfl] selects NFL. Selection precedes the cap or pagination and appears as normalized selection beside the result fields; changed selections cannot share cursors or ETags. Every row carries nullable market_context with nullable league, series_slug, market_type and metadata_updated_at for authoritative filter discovery; metadata_updated_at is the local canonical writer clock, not provider observation time. Selected reads fail closed with 503 read_model_warming if frozen sidecar readiness is absent. Board defaults stay B grade floor, 30 rows and 48-hour horizon; min_grade S/A/B and limit clamp 1..30 are configurable, total is before the cap, with both current outcome quotes. Signals use min_grade default B, horizon default 12/clamp 1..48, limit default 20/clamp 1..100 and cursor, retaining token_id, all ranked/holder/directional/category-skill fields and clocks. Grade floor requires a holder at that grade or better without removing other holders. Observations require cohort wider_holder|in_play|emerging_pile, accept limit/cursor, and retain full observation rows, snapshot_as_of, degraded, source-generation/category funnel diagnostics and REST meta. With cohort wider_holder, admission most_held_48h opts in to the most-held selection instead: per sport, up to 8 wider_holder markets kicking off within 48 hours, most graded holders first, then volume, then soonest kickoff, at most 4 per event, recomputed every refresh and not held; every row's admitted_by is most_held_48h, the response echoes admission, and its funnel, coverage and degradation describe that selection. Required degradation_reasons names each cause with its canonical sport or null for a generation-wide cause. Degradation and coverage input_markets/capacity_limited_markets/emitted_observations/incomplete_holder_markets describe the whole all-sports generation and remain unchanged by selectors. coverage.selected_observations counts matching selected cohort rows before pagination; returned_observations counts this page. Intentional capacity_limited admission does not itself degrade a snapshot, and pagination cannot recover excluded markets. not_configured upcoming supply is not a provider failure. A selected funnel with no failure terminals does not prove the shared generation healthy. A legacy category value that cannot resolve to a sport retains its zero-work empty result: all six counts are zero and reasons are empty without reading the all-sports snapshot, so those values do not establish its health. Observation horizon stays 48h with 12h in-play kickoff lookback and 30s live snapshot ceiling; after one missed refresh, observations serve the last snapshot up to 45s longer with its age in meta.cache_age_s, and a second miss in a row returns 503; funnel accounting is not a league/type/ID selection census. All public views read warmed generations only; missing or stale readiness returns 503 read_model_warming with Retry-After 5. Advanced views use private,no-cache with REST/SDK ETag/304 helpers; board uses private,no-store and has no ETag/pagination. Invalid mode-specific parameters return 400. Price marks are market midpoints, not wallet entry prices; volume is shares. Null/db_only/degraded identify unavailable or weaker evidence. Analytics is not an order instruction.

kind.description: All views: sports excludes the Esports bucket; esports selects only Esports. Omit for both. Combines with other selections using AND. Selected reads echo normalized selection and require frozen metadata readiness.

sports.description: Canonical sport buckets, including Esports and Table Tennis, matched case-insensitively. Unknown names and league aliases such as NFL are rejected in sports; use category for legacy bucket aliases or leagues for exact league selection. Omission covers every sport admitted by the selected view. All views. Repeat this query key or put comma-separated values inside a value. Values normalize, sort and deduplicate; at most 100 supplied values before deduplication. Values within this axis match OR; different selected axes match AND. An empty selection is invalid. Filtering precedes the board cap or advanced pagination and is bound to advanced cursors and ETags.

leagues.description: Normalized machine/provider league identities, such as nfl, cfb, nba, epl, cs2, lol, dota2 or valorant. Known wire/tag aliases normalize; other provider keys match exact lowercase identity. This is separate from category: category=NFL selects Football, while leagues=nfl selects NFL only. Read market_context.league for authoritative values. All views. Repeat this query key or put comma-separated values inside a value. Values normalize, sort and deduplicate; at most 100 supplied values before deduplication. Values within this axis match OR; different selected axes match AND. An empty selection is invalid. Filtering precedes the board cap or advanced pagination and is bound to advanced cursors and ETags.

market_types.description: Exact provider sports_market_type values. This is an open provider taxonomy, distinct from exact market IDs. Read market_context.market_type; missing selected metadata excludes the row. All views. Repeat this query key or put comma-separated values inside a value. Values normalize, sort and deduplicate; at most 100 supplied values before deduplication. Values within this axis match OR; different selected axes match AND. An empty selection is invalid. Filtering precedes the board cap or advanced pagination and is bound to advanced cursors and ETags.

condition_ids.description: Exact market selections. Raw provider condition IDs and the existing mkt_-prefixed aliases normalize to raw IDs. Unknown well-formed IDs return an empty result. All views. Repeat this query key or put comma-separated values inside a value. Values normalize, sort and deduplicate; at most 100 supplied values before deduplication. Values within this axis match OR; different selected axes match AND. An empty selection is invalid. Filtering precedes the board cap or advanced pagination and is bound to advanced cursors and ETags.

event_slugs.description: Exact provider event slugs. Use event_slug returned on the row; no title or slug-prefix guessing. All views. Repeat this query key or put comma-separated values inside a value. Values normalize, sort and deduplicate; at most 100 supplied values before deduplication. Values within this axis match OR; different selected axes match AND. An empty selection is invalid. Filtering precedes the board cap or advanced pagination and is bound to advanced cursors and ETags.

series_slugs.description: Exact provider series slugs. Read market_context.series_slug; a missing selected series excludes the row. All views. Repeat this query key or put comma-separated values inside a value. Values normalize, sort and deduplicate; at most 100 supplied values before deduplication. Values within this axis match OR; different selected axes match AND. An empty selection is invalid. Filtering precedes the board cap or advanced pagination and is bound to advanced cursors and ETags.

category.description: All views; legacy canonical bucket alias. NFL selects Football; use leagues=[nfl] for NFL only.

cohort.description: Required for observations; rejected for board/signals

admission.description: Observations with cohort wider_holder only: the most-held selection, up to 8 markets per sport within 48 hours, recomputed every refresh. Omit for the default selection

min_grade.description: Board/signals only; holder at this grade or better, default B

limit.description: Board cap default 30/clamp 1..30; advanced page default 20/clamp 1..100

cursor.description: Advanced next_cursor, bound to view, all normalized selections and snapshot

horizon_hours.description: Board default 48/signals default 12, clamp 1..48; rejected for observations

tools.name: list_games
tools.description:
The fixture list: one coherent game per row, so an agent never has to assemble a game from market searches and team-name matching. Each row carries both sides with their provider ids and live scores, the UTC kickoff, the provider's own status, the esports series format, and every linked Polymarket market with its condition_id and outcome token ids. Ordered by kickoff, then event_slug; games whose kickoff the provider has not published sort last.

Args:
  - sport (string, optional): canonical bucket, case-insensitive, with - and _ read as a space (table-tennis and Table Tennis are one bucket). Omitted means every covered sport
  - league (string, optional): league tag as coverage.leagues spells it (nfl, epl, cs2), case-insensitive
  - status (string, optional): scheduled, live, paused, ended, postponed, cancelled, suspended, delayed, or unknown
  - starts_after / starts_before (string, optional): RFC 3339 kickoff bounds; a game with no published kickoff is excluded whenever either bound is set
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20)
  - cursor (string, optional): opaque gms_v1_ cursor from next_cursor. It pins the page position, not a snapshot: the catalog is live, so a game added or removed between pages moves with it

Returns: data, has_more, next_cursor, as_of, coverage and meta. Read coverage before reading an empty page: it names the sports and leagues this deployment serves and any scope whose source was unavailable for this read, so an unserved sport is never confused with a quiet night. A sport or status this deployment does not serve returns an empty page, not an error. status.state keeps postponed, cancelled, suspended and delayed distinct from a plain 'not live', and a kickoff in the past is never read as live on its own. Scores are the provider's own strings, because a set score and a run total are not both integers. Carries no price, no sharp-money split and no holder identity; those stay on get_market_snapshot, get_sharp_money_flows and get_edge_hunter.

sport.description: Canonical sport bucket, case-insensitive, with - and _ read as a space; omitted means every covered sport. A bucket this deployment does not serve returns an empty page

league.description: League tag as coverage.leagues spells it: nfl, epl, cs2. Case-insensitive

status.description: Keep only games in this state

starts_after.description: RFC 3339 instant; keep only games whose kickoff is at or after it

starts_before.description: RFC 3339 instant; keep only games whose kickoff is at or before it. Must be at or after starts_after

cursor.description: Opaque gms_v1_ cursor from next_cursor; it pins the page position (kickoff and event_slug), not a snapshot

tools.name: get_game
tools.description:
The same game object list_games returns, for one event_slug: both sides with their provider ids and live scores, the UTC kickoff, the provider's own status, the esports series format, and every linked Polymarket market with its condition_id and outcome token ids. The slug is the identity the live_sports_updated webhook pulse carries, so a receiver can read the full game straight from a pulse.

Args:
  - event_slug (string, required): the game's event slug, for example nfl-buf-nyj-2026-09-22. Matched case-insensitively

Returns: the game object with the envelope's meta. status.state keeps postponed, cancelled, suspended and delayed distinct from a plain 'not live'. Each game's own coverage reports whether scores, competitor provider ids and the schedule were available: when competitors reads labels, do not join on names. A slug outside the published coverage answers 404, including a real Polymarket event in a sport this deployment does not serve; list_games names what is covered. Carries no price, no sharp-money split and no holder identity.

event_slug.description: The game's event slug, for example nfl-buf-nyj-2026-09-22; matched case-insensitively

tools.name: get_market_flow
tools.description:
One market's flow and top positions: the signed flow of every tracked large trade in the window (net_flow_usd and its direction, YES or NO), the large-trade count, gross buy and sell volumes, and the top five graded trader positions. The envelope object is market_flow.

Use search_markets first to find the condition_id for a market.

Args:
  - condition_id (string, required): Market condition ID (from search_markets results)
  - timeframe (string, optional): Lookback window: "1h", "4h", "24h", "7d" (default "24h")

Returns: Market info, the flow under sharp_money (net_flow_usd, direction YES/NO, large_trade_count, volumes) with smart_money as its deprecated byte-identical alias, and the top 5 graded trader positions.

tools.name: get_pick_of_the_day
tools.description:
Get today's published Pick of the Day selections and their recorded facts. Pro opens five selections in total: the explicitly designated free selection plus the first four non-free selections in publication order. Max opens every available daily selection, up to twenty. Read entitled `picks` in `publication_order` order; use stable decimal-string `pick_id` for identity, not deprecated `pick_rank`. `is_free_selection` designates account access; `supersedes_pick_id` is deprecated and always null. `locked_picks` lists extra unresolved slots with only pick_rank and required_tier=max; game identity, identifying clocks and backed facts are omitted. Each full pick carries the matchup, backed side (pick_outcome_label), recorded publication price and return on the flat $1,000 stake (`stake_usd`, `return_usd`; `return_per_100` keeps the literal $100 basis), available holder facts, top grade, CLV capture status and backend-provided thesis. `scheduled_picks` contains entitled scheduled slots with release_at and kickoff; unauthorized slots appear in identity-free locked_picks instead. No market identity is revealed before publication. Withdrawn picks are omitted from current and dated recommendations, the archive and its statistics, even after market settlement. The public ledger retains every published commitment under its original identity and proof bytes.

When no active pick is available, the tool returns reason pick_not_released and retry_at. Schedule the next read from the returned retry guidance or an entitled scheduled slot's release_at instead of polling. An entitled published pick whose holder proof is not readable appears in `proof_pending_picks` (pick_rank, release_at, kickoff, retry_at), while `picks` contains readable picks. The tool returns read_model_warming only when no entitled published pick has readable proof. If only Max-locked selections have published, a successful state=none response carries picks=[], pick_count=0, locked_picks and an upgrade action.

For automated entry, require a present, matching, unexpired entry_authorization. Honor its returned max_entry_price and expires_at, quote a current executable book for the actual stake and retain any stricter local limits. Fees are separate; authorization guarantees neither liquidity nor execution.

Args: none

Returns: The published pick set for the current product day (America/New_York), or a pick_not_released error with retry_at.

tools.name: get_pick_of_the_day_ledger_entry
tools.description: Read one published pick's sealed, opened or uncommitted ledger entry by its stable decimal-string pick_id. commitment_version explicitly selects version 1 legacy proofs or version 2 rank-free proofs. Never infer a proof format from dates or reorder canonical bytes. Pending proofs withhold the backed side and nonce. This tool requires the usual authenticated MCP tools/call transport; the corresponding REST read is public.

pick_id.description: Stable positive database row id as decimal text

tools.name: get_pick_of_the_day_archive
tools.description:
Get the Pick of the Day track record: each published pick that has not been withdrawn, with its outcome (win, loss, void or pending), recorded publication price, unit score and CLV fields, plus the rolling hit rate (wins / decided; void and pending excluded) and flat-$1,000-stake profit and ROI (`hit_rate.stake_usd` names the stake). The actual API key tier controls unresolved access: Pro opens five selections in total, the designated free selection plus the first four non-free selections in publication order; Max opens every available daily selection, up to twenty. Every resolved outcome (win/loss/void) is public. Unentitled pending rows retain only slot/date/outcome and required_tier with backed_side_locked=true; matchup, category, league, image, publication clock and backed facts are omitted. The archive retains the included historical picks, losses included. Withdrawn recommendations are omitted from archive rows and every aggregate, including the cumulative series, even after market settlement. The public ledger retains every published commitment under its original pick_id and proof bytes.

Args: none

Returns: picks[] newest first with outcome and CLV fields, plus the aggregate record (hit_rate, decided, wins, losses, voids, profit, roi, total risked).

A wallet address with no trader yet returns sync_status "unknown" on the nested trader; a username or trader id that matches no trader is a not_found error.

Args:

The Esports record also lists each esports game it has a settled market in. The basis is every settled market at any size, so it differs from get_trader's categories expansion, which applies a 20 USD notional floor and an entry-price rule; neither corrects the other. A category with fewer decided markets than min_decided_for_win_rate keeps its counts with win_rate null and status not_enough_data. An absent category means no record, never a 0% record.

Args:

  - category (string, optional): One canonical category through the shared rollup: soccer and EPL reach Soccer, every esports label reaches Esports, football is American football. A game is not a filter: ask for esports and read games

Returns: records, min_decided_for_win_rate, basis, computed_at and meta. A trader with no settled market returns empty records; an unknown address is a not_found error.

tools.description:
The grade a trader was visibly recorded with at a past instant, from prospective grade observations: what the wallet's grade was when a trade or decision happened, never a reconstruction. status is graded, ungraded or unknown; use grade only when status is graded. Before available_from (the first recorded observation), after deletion, or in a grade-transition gap, status is unknown and grade is null. observation carries observed_at, published_by and model provenance, which older observations leave null. Never substitute a current grade.

Args:
  - address (string, required): Wallet address (0x...), username, or trd_-prefixed trader id
  - as_of (string, required): RFC3339 instant, such as the trade or decision time; future instants are refused

Returns: status, grade, available_from, observation and meta.

address.description: Wallet address (0x...), username, or trd_-prefixed trader id

as_of.description: RFC3339 instant whose recorded grade is read, such as the trade or decision time; future instants are refused

tools.name: get_market_holders
tools.description:
The S, A and B graded wallets holding one Polymarket market, from a complete provider holder scan: shares, Polymarket's currentValue for the leg, grade, win record in the market's category, and badges. A wallet holding both outcomes is listed once on its net side. Ordered by current value. The roster is at most 60 seconds old over a provider walk at most 180 seconds old; scan.fetched_at is its only timestamp. An incomplete scan is an error with a retry time, never a shorter list. C, D, F and ungraded wallets are never listed and are counted only in scan.wallet_count. Counts differ from get_positions by design: a live scan, the graded cohort, and no 100 USD size floor.

Args:
  - condition_id (string, required): Raw provider condition_id or the mkt_-prefixed market id
  - outcome (string, optional): yes, no, or all (default)
  - min_grade (string, optional): S keeps S, A keeps S and A, B (default) keeps S, A and B
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20): Holders per page
  - cursor (string, optional): next_cursor from the previous page, bound to the same market and filters

Returns: data (holders), has_more, next_cursor, total, market, scan, totals and meta.

condition_id.description: Raw provider condition_id or the mkt_-prefixed market id

outcome.description: Keep holders netting one side; all (the default) lists both

min_grade.description: Narrow the graded cohort: S keeps S, A keeps S and A, B (the default) keeps S, A and B

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; it is bound to the same market and filters

tools.name: get_market_candles
tools.description:
OHLC price candles for a market's outcome tokens from the stored Polymarket CLOB price history, the series the market chart draws, for open and resolved markets. The stored series is daily: a 1d candle usually holds one point, so its open, high, low and close are that day's close, and 1w aggregates the daily closes. No intraday detail is invented.

Args:
  - condition_id (string, required): Raw provider condition_id or the mkt_-prefixed market id
  - resolution (string, optional): 1d (default, UTC day) or 1w (ISO week from Monday 00:00 UTC)
  - from (integer, optional): Exclusive lower bound, unix seconds
  - to (integer, optional): Inclusive upper bound, unix seconds; from must not be after to

Returns: condition_id, resolution, and outcomes, each with its token_id and candles, plus meta.

condition_id.description: Raw provider condition_id or the mkt_-prefixed market id

resolution.description: 1d (the default) buckets by UTC day, 1w by ISO week from Monday 00:00 UTC

from.description: Exclusive lower bound in unix seconds

to.description: Inclusive upper bound in unix seconds; from must not be after to

tools.name: get_combo_fills
tools.description:
Live Polymarket combo (multi-leg) taker fills with exact decimal-string economics, wallet identity and grade, legs, conjunction result and ingest coverage. Requires a Pro or Max API key. The listing holds executions priced at most 0.95; get_combo has a combo's complete history. sort recent pages with next_cursor; largest and payout page with next_offset. A continuation can end on an empty page.

Args:
  - result (string, optional): CSV of pending, won, lost; all clears the filter
  - legs (string, optional): CSV of 2, 3, 4, 5+; all clears the filter
  - min_stake (integer, optional, default 0): Minimum collateral in whole USDC
  - min_multiplier (integer, optional, default 0): 0 disables the filter; otherwise 2 to 1000000 shares per dollar at execution
  - grades (string, optional): CSV of S, A, B, C, D, F; all clears the filter; ungraded wallets never match
  - sports (string, optional): CSV of sport slugs such as nfl, nba, soccer, esports; all clears the filter; a combo matches when any leg is in a selected sport
  - sort (string, optional): recent (default, newest first), largest (collateral), or payout (buy-fill shares, sells excluded)
  - window (string, optional): 24h, 7d or all; defaults to all for recent and 24h for largest and payout
  - limit (number, 1-200, default 50): Fills per page
  - cursor (string, optional): next_cursor from the previous recent page
  - offset (number, 0-5000, optional): next_offset from the previous largest or payout page

Returns: data (fills), has_more, next_cursor, next_offset, limit, sort, window, coverage and meta.

result.description: CSV of pending, won, lost; all clears the filter

legs.description: CSV of 2, 3, 4, 5+; all clears the filter. A combo matches any named pick count

min_multiplier.description: Minimum shares per dollar at execution: 0 (the default) disables the filter, otherwise 2 to 1000000

grades.description: CSV of S, A, B, C, D, F; all clears the filter. Ungraded wallets never match

sports.description: CSV of sport slugs such as nfl, nba, soccer, esports; all clears the filter. A combo matches when any leg is in a selected sport

sort.description: recent (the default) is newest first; largest ranks collateral; payout ranks buy-fill shares and excludes sells

window.description: Defaults to all for recent and 24h for largest and payout

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; recent ordering only

offset.description: next_offset from the previous page; largest and payout ordering only

tools.name: get_combos_summary
tools.description:
The stored count of traded Polymarket combos whose YES conjunction is still pending, and when it was computed. Requires a Pro or Max API key. The count refreshes at most every five minutes and is cached for 60 seconds. A null live value is unknown, never zero.

Returns: live (count and computed_at, or null) and meta.

tools.name: get_combo
tools.description:
One Polymarket combo: legs, conjunction result, all-time trade totals, the newest 100 taker fills, lifecycle totals and ingest coverage. Requires a Pro or Max API key. Unlike get_combo_fills it keeps executions priced above 0.95. Null lifecycle or missing leg facts are unknown, never zero.

Args:
  - condition_id (string, required): Combo ID, 0x and 62 lowercase hex characters; not a binary market's condition_id

Returns: combo, fills, lifecycle, coverage, access and meta. A malformed ID is a bad_request error and an unknown one not_found.

condition_id.description: Combo ID: 0x and 62 lowercase hex characters, not a binary market's condition_id

tools.name: get_large_trade_counterparty_executions
tools.description:
Page the counterparty executions of one large trade past the first page get_large_trade embeds in counterparty_analysis. Reads the immutable snapshot that response names; a stale or changed snapshot fails with reason cursor_expired, so read get_large_trade again and restart.

Args:
  - id (string, required): Large trade ID such as wt_123 or 123
  - snapshot_id (string, required): counterparty_analysis.snapshot_id from get_large_trade
  - cursor (string, optional): executions_next_cursor from get_large_trade or from the previous page
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 100): Executions per page

Returns: executions (each with its first makers page and makers_next_cursor), executions_next_cursor, execution counts, status and meta.

cursor.description: executions_next_cursor from get_large_trade or from the previous page

tools.name: get_large_trade_counterparty_makers

Page the maker wallets of one counterparty execution past the first page its execution embeds. Percentages keep the whole execution as their denominator across pages.

  - snapshot_id (string, required): counterparty_analysis.snapshot_id from get_large_trade
  - cursor (string, optional): makers_next_cursor from the execution or next_cursor from the previous page
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 100): Makers per page

Returns: items (makers), next_cursor, execution_id, snapshot_id and meta.
